question.problem:
Find the equation of the **normal** line to the polar curve $r=1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ at $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3}$ given that

$$
{y}^{′}(\theta )=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ),\,{x}^{′}(\theta )=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$
question.worked_solution:
To find the equation of the normal line to a polar curve at a point $P,$ we follow four steps:

**Step 1**: Calculate the derivative $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

In this case, we're given that

$$
{y}^{′}(\theta )=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ),\,{x}^{′}(\theta )=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Find the slope of the tangent at $P:$

The slope of the tangent line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =2\pi /3} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{2\pi }{3})}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{2\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3})}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{1}{2}-2\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})}{2\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{(-\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2})} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P:$

We compute the $xy$-coordinates of $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}))\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}) \\  & =(1-2(-\frac{1}{2}))(-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-1 \\ {y}_{1} & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}))\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}) \\  & =(1-2(-\frac{1}{2}))\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $(-1,\sqrt{3}).$

**Step 4**: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the normal:

We find the equation of the normal as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{m}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-\sqrt{3} & =3\sqrt{3}\cdot (x-(-1)) \\ y-\sqrt{3} & =3\sqrt{3}x+3\sqrt{3} \\ y & =3\sqrt{3}x+4\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$
